title: Admissibility of integral compactification refinement diagrams
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ and a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No absolute separatedness of the schemes is imposed. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories $C_s(T)=D^b_{ctf}(T,s)$ [def-sf-categories], completed at integral stages and with positive finite levels $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\ge1$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].
Fix $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$ and $A_n=R/t^n$. For a finite-type $k$-scheme $W$ put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves, with transitions $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$. Use their derived categories, the canonical reduction system $\mathcal R_W K$, exact termwise open extension $J_j$, and total derived system proper direct image $S_p$ [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. A system is normalized if every transition-adjoint $M_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to M_n$ is invertible.

Let $K\in C_{R}(X)$ and suppose all its reductions have Tor amplitude in one interval $[a,b]$. Choose an identity or binary compactification-refinement diagram for $f$, with quasi-compact open factors $j_c$, proper factors $p_c$ and proper refinements $u,v$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Consider every intermediate system obtained from $\mathcal R_XK$ along any of the finitely many words in $J_j,S_p$ in that diagram, including hidden open intermediates in $S_{p_c}J_{j_c}$ and the refinement proper images.

Every such intermediate system is normalized, has constructible levels with a common finite cohomological interval and a common finite Tor interval independent of $n$, and has bounded etale-origin witnesses compatible with its actual coefficient transitions. More precisely an open extension preserves a chosen Tor interval; a proper factor with source dimension bounded by $d\ge0$ sends $[a',b']$ into $[a',b'+2d]$. All sources have finite dimension, and $d=0$ is admissible for an empty source. A single common upper bound can be chosen for the finite collection of words. Each intermediate system is canonically identified, with its quotient transitions, with the reduction system of the corresponding derived-complete constructible integral intermediate object. These are the intermediate-domain conditions of [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain], so the realization isomorphisms $c_V$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] apply to this whole identity or binary refinement diagram.

proof.text: Check the eighteen constructors explicitly: every word is a support word and geometric. Proper ambient structure maps are compositions of proper maps with the finite-type structure map of Y; this requires no structural separatedness. Apply the source uniform field-extension dimension bound to each output structural map, specializing to the identity pullback over the coefficient field. Take the finite maximum of the eighteen natural bounds.

Apply completedShriekIntegralBounds to each geometric support word. This supplies the full recursive expression domain (including all hidden open prefixes, normalization, bounds, and the actual compatible origins) and integral constructibility of its integral interpretation. The helper is an already proved declaration of the composition-laws node; it imposes no absolute separatedness hypothesis and does not depend on this refinement admissibility node.

Derive sharp local estimates from the existing finite-level statements. For an open immersion, apply finiteStageDerivedExtensionByZero_constructibleFiniteTor with any chosen input Tor interval, using level constructibility from Good. Transport its interval along the specified openEvaluation isomorphism. For a proper arrow with any nonnegative source dimension bound d, apply finiteCoefficientDirectImage_boundedConstructible_torAmplitude and transport [a,b+2d] along the specified direct-image evaluation. Isomorphism invariance is proved directly from the explicit resolution-based Tor definition.

Induct on support-word syntax with the fixed lower endpoint a. The variable uses the assumed [a,b] interval transported across reductionEvaluation. An open constructor retains the current upper endpoint. A proper constructor adds twice its source dimension bound. A compact-support constructor performs the open and proper steps separately; its hidden open system is Good by the recursive domain already obtained in step 2. The same induction retains the universal sharp estimates at the last constructor. Pullback and tensor cases are excluded by the support-word hypothesis.

Choose an upper endpoint for each of the eighteen words and a common upper bound for their finite range. Widen every Tor interval directly in its resolution-based definition. For cohomological support, apply the bounded-flat-model theorem to each constructible finite level; its representative is zero outside [a,B], hence exact there, so homology vanishes outside [a,B]. The prime is invertible in each residue field by the finite-field prime-unit theorem and the structural residue-field map. The proof handles zero inputs and empty schemes without an additional hypothesis.

For every word use the geometric and domain witnesses and integral constructibility from step 2. Precompose the supplied Realizations.normalization equation by reduction(comparison.inv). Functoriality and comparison.inv_hom cancel that factor against reduction(comparison.hom), leaving the desired equality of actual derived-system maps. Thus all quotient transitions are retained; no equality is inferred only from finite evaluations.
